acid-deposition.def: Acids that fall from the air in rain, snow or fog (wet deposition) or as dry particles and gases (dry deposition). It forms when sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides react in the air to make sulfuric and nitric acid. Often called acid rain.

buffering.def: Buffering capacity: the ability of soil, rock or water to neutralize acid and resist a change in pH. Limestone gives lakes and soils a high buffering capacity; granite gives little.
